newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: BASS SAYS STILL TALKING ON CZECH RADEGAST.
newsitem.headline: BASS SAYS STILL TALKING ON CZECH RADEGAST.

text.p: Britain's Bass Plc denied an unsourced report in the Czech press that it was about to buy a 34 percent stake in brewer Radegast a.s. from Radegast's largest shareholder IPB Banka a.s. .

Bass country manager Mervyn Childs told Reuters on Tuesday that his company, which already holds a 33 percent stake in Radegast, hoped that talks with IPB on the Radegast stake would bear fruit in the near future, but that nothing was imminent.
"Discussions are carrying on and we hope to reach some agreement but I can't say much else because there's almost nothing further to say," said Childs.

On Monday, Czech business daily Hospodarske Noviny quoted an unnamned source as saying that an agreement with IPB had almost been reached. Asked whether the report had any substance, Childs said, "No."
Bass's attempt to increase its holding in Radegast is part of a broader strategy to create a major Czech brewing group controlling around 25-30 percent of the domestic beer market.
Bass already holds a 55 percent stake in Prague Breweries a.s whose premium brand Staropramen, is sold in most major European countries.

Childs has said previously that Bass would contemplate the posssibility of a mega-merger between Radegast, which controls around 16 percent of the Czech beer market, and Prague Breweries, which controls around 14 percent, if it is able to acquire a larger stake in Radegast.
